Measured connectivity for 22,900 haloes (10¹²-10¹⁵.⁵ h⁻¹M⊙), finding power-law mass-connectivity relation extending from group to cluster scales.
AI.conclusion: The method successfully overcomes DisPerSE's memory bottleneck while preserving global topology, enabling large-scale filament reconstruction. Provides first N-body confirmation that theoretically predicted scaling holds across three decades in halo mass.

title: Probabilistic redshift estimation of unresolved galaxies from multi-band background light maps
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 2 tables
summary: Accurate knowledge of the redshift distributions of unresolved galaxy populations is essential for extracting the cosmological information encoded in the cosmic optical background. We present the first framework for estimating these distributions directly from multi-band maps of unresolved background light, using conditional normalising flows trained on realistic image simulations. For imaging qualities comparable to those expected from the synergy between the Euclid and Rubin LSST surveys, our model achieves sub-per cent accuracy in both the mean and standard deviation of the flux-weighted redshift distributions when the training and target samples are statistically well matched. Furthermore, the network proves highly resilient to incomplete photometric coverage when combined with tailored data imputation strategies. To address the challenge of statistical mismatches between simulations and real observations, we propose incorporating observational quantities into the target variables, providing a built-in diagnostic to assess model reliability and uncertainty from the predictions themselves. We also demonstrate the feasibility of map-based tomographic analyses, showing that the model retains sufficient pixel-level detail to recover redshift distributions for tomographically defined subsamples with near sub-per cent accuracy across all bins. These results establish conditional normalising flows as a viable tool for redshift estimation of unresolved sources, opening new opportunities for component separation, signal interpretation, and cosmological inference using multi-band optical background fluctuations.

AI.tldr: The paper presents the first framework using conditional normalising flows on simulated multi-band maps to estimate flux-weighted redshift distributions of unresolved galaxy populations, achieving sub-per cent accuracy, resilience to incomplete data, and enabling tomographic analyses for cosmological inference from the cosmic optical background.
AI.motivation: Accurate redshift distributions of unresolved galaxy populations are essential for extracting cosmological information from the cosmic optical background, but existing methods cannot estimate these distributions directly from multi-band maps of unresolved background light.
AI.method: Conditional normalising flows trained on realistic image simulations are used to estimate flux-weighted redshift distributions directly from multi-band maps of unresolved background light.
AI.result: Sub-per cent accuracy in mean and standard deviation of flux-weighted redshift distributions under well-matched training/target samples; high resilience to incomplete photometric coverage via tailored imputation; observational quantities integrated as target variables for built-in diagnostic; tomographic analyses achieve near sub-per cent accuracy across all bins.
AI.conclusion: Conditional normalising flows are a viable tool for redshift estimation of unresolved sources, enabling component separation, signal interpretation, and cosmological inference using multi-band optical background fluctuations.

title: Fuelling the central region of galaxies with misaligned gas accretion
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. 15 pages, 13 figures
summary: Recent studies have shown that the accretion of kinematically misaligned gas fuels the central reservoir of galaxies, triggering nuclear activity and star formation. In this work, we show that this specific accretion channel can only sustain main-sequence levels of star formation in galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^{10} {\rm M_\odot}$. Using a sample of 201 kinematically misaligned galaxies, and a comparison sample of 3689 aligned galaxies, from the Mapping Nearby Galaxies at Apache Point Observatory survey, we investigate the impact of kinematically misaligned gas on star formation across stellar mass. We characterise the global specific star formation rate, central concentration and mass of ionized gas of our samples, and derive radial profiles of specific star formation rate and ionized gas mass surface density. We find that misaligned galaxies exhibit more centrally concentrated ionized gas than their aligned counterparts, with the strongest enhancement occurring at intermediate masses ($10^{10}$-$10^{10.6} {\rm M_\odot}$), where the central ionized gas density peaks. In galaxies less massive than $10^{10} {\rm M_\odot}$, misaligned gas fuels nuclear star formation at rates typical of star-forming systems. At higher masses, however, the impact of this newly accreted gas is diluted by the larger pre-existing stellar mass in the central regions, limiting its ability to rejuvenate the star formation activity in these galaxies. Our results also show that misaligned galaxies with or without nuclear activity exhibit similar central concentrations of ionized gas, suggesting that most have a reservoir capable of fuelling their supermassive black holes over timescales longer than typical nuclear activity episodes.

AI.tldr: Using 201 kinematically misaligned and 3689 aligned galaxies from the MaNGA survey, the study finds that misaligned gas accretion sustains main-sequence star formation only in galaxies with $M_* \lesssim 10^{10} \, M_\odot$. At higher masses, the accreted gas is diluted by pre-existing stellar mass, limiting its impact on star formation rejuvenation. Misaligned galaxies show more centrally concentrated ionized gas, and those with or without nuclear activity have similar central gas concentrations, indicating a persistent fuel reservoir for supermassive black holes.
AI.motivation: To understand how kinematically misaligned gas accretion influences star formation and nuclear activity across different galaxy stellar masses, and to determine the mass regime where this accretion channel is effective.
AI.method: Analyzed a sample of 201 kinematically misaligned galaxies and 3689 aligned galaxies from the MaNGA survey, characterizing global specific star formation rate (sSFR), central concentration, and ionized gas mass, alongside radial profiles of sSFR and ionized gas mass surface density.
AI.result: Misaligned galaxies sustain main-sequence star formation only below $M_* \lesssim 10^{10} \, M_\odot$. At intermediate masses ($10^{10}$–$10^{10.6} \, M_\odot$), central ionized gas density peaks. Above $10^{10} \, M_\odot$, accreted gas is diluted by pre-existing stellar mass. Misaligned galaxies with and without nuclear activity show similar central gas concentrations.
AI.conclusion: Kinematically misaligned gas accretion is an effective fuel source for star formation only in lower-mass galaxies; in massive galaxies, its impact on star formation rejuvenation is limited. The persistent central gas reservoir in misaligned galaxies can sustain supermassive black hole fueling over long timescales.

title: Pushing the Primordial Frontier: Cosmological Collider Signatures at Strong Mixing
comment: 24 pages
summary: We develop an analytic treatment of primordial non-Gaussianity in multifield inflation that is nonperturbative in the constant curvature--isocurvature mixing strength $λ$. Using exact linear solutions for the coupled curvature perturbation $ζ$ and isocurvature perturbation $σ$, we construct dressed propagators and derive exact integral representations for the tree-level bispectra generated by the interactions $\dotζ^2σ$, $\dotζ\,σ^2$, and $σ^3$. This formalism resums curvature--isocurvature transfer to all orders in $λ$ and applies for arbitrary values of the entropy mass $μ$. We obtain closed-form expressions for the leading squeezed limit of the bispectrum contributions and recover the well-known cosmological-collider and quasi-single-field results in the weak-mixing limit. In the strong-mixing regime, where conventional transfer perturbation theory breaks down, we find that both the power spectrum and the bispectrum can be dramatically enhanced, giving rise to distinctive nonperturbative scaling laws for the reduced non-Gaussian amplitude. Together, these results open a new analytic window onto multifield inflation beyond the weak-coupling approximation and establish a framework for studying cosmological-collider signals, primordial-black-hole production, and loop corrections in strongly mixed inflationary dynamics.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a nonperturbative analytic framework for primordial non-Gaussianity in multifield inflation, resumming curvature-isocurvature mixing to all orders and obtaining closed-form bispectra in the squeezed limit, revealing enhanced power spectra and bispectra with distinctive scaling laws in the strong-mixing regime.
AI.motivation: To go beyond the weak-coupling approximation in multifield inflation and provide a nonperturbative analytic treatment of primordial non-Gaussianity that works for arbitrarily strong curvature-isocurvature mixing, where conventional perturbation theory fails.
AI.method: Using exact linear solutions for the coupled curvature perturbation ζ and isocurvature perturbation σ, the authors construct dressed propagators and derive exact integral representations for tree-level bispectra generated by the interactions ζ̇²σ, ζ̇σ², and σ³, resumming curvature-isocurvature transfer to all orders in the mixing strength λ for arbitrary entropy mass μ.
AI.result: Closed-form expressions for the leading squeezed limit of bispectrum contributions are obtained, recovering cosmological-collider and quasi-single-field results in the weak-mixing limit. In the strong-mixing regime, both power spectrum and bispectrum are dramatically enhanced with distinct nonperturbative scaling laws for the reduced non-Gaussian amplitude fNL.
AI.conclusion: This work opens a new analytic window onto multifield inflation beyond weak coupling, establishing a framework for studying cosmological-collider signals, primordial-black-hole production, and loop corrections in strongly mixed inflationary dynamics.

title: Discrepancies between Chandrasekhar's theory of relaxation and $N$-body simulations
comment: 13 pages, 12 figures, 3 tables, submitted to A&A
summary: Globular clusters are systems which are known to be particularly well described by two-body relaxation. In recent decades many studies have shown that Chandrasekhar's orbit-averaged theory is able to reproduce many features of numerical simulations. However, it has been claimed that differences between the theory and simulation remain, such as an amplitude mismatch of the rate of change of the distribution function. In this paper we compare the theoretical predictions of Chandrasekhar's theory for anisotropic clusters to precise $N$-body data. We show that more careful $N$-body measurements are able to reduce the claimed mismatch. Nevertheless, we observe a dependency of the remaining mismatch on both position and anisotropy. While the dependence on anisotropy may be understood qualitatively on theoretical grounds, the radial dependence implies that spatial inhomogeneities, and therefore collective effects, may become unavoidable to resolve the residual mismatch between theory and simulations.

AI.tldr: This paper tests Chandrasekhar's orbit-averaged theory against precise N-body simulations of globular clusters, finding that careful measurements reduce but do not eliminate mismatches, which depend on position and anisotropy, suggesting collective effects may be needed to fully resolve discrepancies.
AI.motivation: To resolve the claimed amplitude mismatch between Chandrasekhar's orbit-averaged theory and numerical simulations of two-body relaxation in globular clusters.
AI.method: Comparison of Chandrasekhar's theoretical predictions for anisotropic clusters with precise N-body data, using more careful measurements to reduce systematic errors.
AI.result: More careful N-body measurements reduce the claimed mismatch; however, residual mismatch depends on both position (radial coordinate) and anisotropy, with the radial dependence suggesting collective effects are at play.
AI.conclusion: Spatial inhomogeneities and collective effects may be unavoidable to fully resolve the residual mismatch between Chandrasekhar's theory and simulations.

title: Probing Graviton Mass with MeerKAT PTA and SKA--PTA Forecasts
comment: 12 pages, 4 figures
summary: We present constraints on the graviton mass using the 4.5-year data release from the MeerKAT Pulsar Timing Array (MPTA) and provide forecasts for the upcoming Square Kilometre Array PTA (SKA--PTA). By modeling the modified dispersion relation and the corresponding tensor correlation function for massive gravitons, we perform Bayesian inference on the angular-correlation measurements under three noise configurations (DATA, ER, ALT). Our 90\% credible upper limits on the graviton mass are $m_g < 2.10 \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (DATA), $m_g < 2.58 \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (ER), and $m_g < 2.25 \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (ALT). Including monopolar and dipolar contributions does not significantly alter these bounds, confirming that the constraints are driven by the quadrupolar tensor correlation. All results remain fully consistent with general relativity. For SKA--PTA, we forecast sensitivities down to $m_g \sim 10^{-24}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 10-year observing baseline and $m_g \sim 10^{-25}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ with a 50-year observing baseline, representing order-of-magnitude improvements over current limits. This work demonstrates the power of current and future PTA observations to test fundamental aspects of gravity in the nanohertz band.

AI.tldr: Using MeerKAT PTA data (4.5 years), Bayesian inference on angular-correlation measurements yields graviton mass upper limits of $m_g < 2.10-2.58 \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (90% credible), consistent with GR. SKA-PTA forecasts predict sensitivities down to $10^{-24}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (10 yr) and $10^{-25}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (50 yr).
AI.motivation: To constrain the graviton mass using pulsar timing array observations, testing the fundamental nature of gravity in the nanohertz band by exploiting the modified dispersion relation and correlation signatures of massive gravitons.
AI.method: Model massive graviton dispersion and tensor correlation function; perform Bayesian inference on angular-correlation measurements under three noise configurations (DATA, ER, ALT); include monopolar and dipolar contributions; forecast SKA-PTA sensitivity.
AI.result: 90% credible upper limits: $m_g < 2.10 \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (DATA), $<2.58 \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (ER), $<2.25 \times 10^{-23}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (ALT); SKA-PTA forecasts $10^{-24}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (10 yr) and $10^{-25}\,\mathrm{eV}/c^{2}$ (50 yr).
AI.conclusion: Current PTA constraints are consistent with GR; future SKA-PTA observations will improve limits by orders of magnitude, demonstrating the power of nanohertz gravitational-wave observations for testing gravity.

title: The COLIBRE-SKIRT pipeline: Calibration-free dust radiative transfer postprocessing for cosmological simulations
comment: Main text 23 pages and 8 figures. Submitted to A&A
summary: Context. Three-dimensional dust radiative transfer provides a powerful framework to connect cosmological galaxy simulations to multiwavelength observations. Until recently, in large-volume simulations, the formation of a cold ISM phase was prevented and dust was not evolved self-consistently. This required calibration of dust-to-metal ratios and extra subgrid dust attenuation in birth clouds, thereby reducing the predictive power. Aims. We present the COLIBRE-SKIRT pipeline, a calibration-free dust radiative transfer framework for the novel COLIBRE suite of large-volume cosmological simulations, which include a live dust model and directly simulate the multiphase ISM. Our primary aim is to establish a reference pipeline for generating multiwavelength mock observables from these simulations. As a first application, we produce far-ultraviolet (FUV) to far-infrared (FIR) spatially integrated spectra and assess them by comparison with the observed low-redshift cosmic spectral energy distribution (CSED). Methods. We apply the SKIRT dust radiative transfer code to the COLIBRE simulations. Dust masses and species fractions are taken directly from the simulation, and no birth cloud model is added in postprocessing. We introduce a "split & scale" approach that maps the simulated two-size, multi-species dust distribution onto continuous grain size distributions without introducing free parameters. Results. We find that, for the first time, a large-volume cosmological simulation directly reproduces the local Universe CSED without calibrating the postprocessing routine a priori. Residual tensions in the mid-infrared (~0.2 dex) point towards insufficient heating of the hottest dust components and uncertainties in the modelling of the PAH-emission carriers. This framework can be readily applied at low and high redshift to create synthetic spectra and images from the FUV to the FIR.

AI.tldr: The COLIBRE-SKIRT pipeline is a calibration-free dust radiative transfer framework for large-volume cosmological simulations that directly reproduces the local Universe cosmic spectral energy distribution from FUV to FIR without needing a priori calibration, using a novel "split & scale" approach to map simulated dust distributions onto continuous grain size distributions.
AI.motivation: Previous large-volume cosmological simulations required calibration of dust-to-metal ratios and extra subgrid dust attenuation in birth clouds because they lacked a cold ISM phase and self-consistent dust evolution, reducing predictive power. This work aims to establish a calibration-free reference pipeline for the COLIBRE simulations that include a live dust model and directly simulate the multiphase ISM.
AI.method: The authors apply the SKIRT dust radiative transfer code to COLIBRE simulations, taking dust masses and species fractions directly from the simulation without adding a birth cloud model in postprocessing. They introduce a "split & scale" approach that maps the simulated two-size, multi-species dust distribution onto continuous grain size distributions without introducing free parameters.
AI.result: For the first time, a large-volume cosmological simulation directly reproduces the local Universe CSED without calibrating the postprocessing routine a priori. Residual tensions in the mid-infrared (~0.2 dex) indicate insufficient heating of the hottest dust components and uncertainties in PAH-emission carrier modelling.
AI.conclusion: The COLIBRE-SKIRT pipeline provides a calibration-free framework that can be readily applied at low and high redshift to create synthetic spectra and images from FUV to FIR, offering improved predictive power for connecting cosmological galaxy simulations to multiwavelength observations.

title: Analytical covariances for catalogue-based pseudo-$C_\ell$s
comment: 29 pages, 9 figures
summary: Multiple cosmological observables, such as the galaxy overdensity or cosmic shear, consist of fields sampled at the discrete positions of astrophysical sources. Recent work has presented methods to estimate the angular power spectra of such fields, avoiding the construction of pixelated sky maps and the finite-resolution effects associated with them. In this work, we present a method to estimate the disconnected (also known as "Gaussian") covariance of these angular power spectra, addressing subtle effects such as the effective area overlap between different catalogue-based fields and the additional Poisson-like variance arising from the discrete nature of the catalogues. The method relies on the so-called Narrow-Kernel Approximation to account for the contribution of distinct source pairs to the estimator, while including the noise-like contributions from self-pairs exactly. We explicitly compare this approach with a brute-force method that can produce the exact covariance for sparse samples, and validate it against simulations. We show that the method is accurate in realistic scenarios, spanning both dense and noise-dominated datasets (e.g., cosmic shear) and sparse, noise-dominated observables (e.g., fast radio bursts). The method is implemented in the public code NaMaster.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a method to estimate the disconnected (Gaussian) covariance of angular power spectra from discrete cosmological fields (e.g., galaxy overdensity, cosmic shear), using the Narrow-Kernel Approximation to handle distinct source pairs and exact treatment of self-pairs. The method is validated against brute-force calculations and simulations, works for both dense and sparse datasets, and is implemented in the public code NaMaster.
AI.motivation: Cosmological observables like galaxy overdensity and cosmic shear are sampled at discrete source positions. Recent work has enabled angular power spectrum estimation without pixelated maps; however, accurately estimating the covariance of these power spectra—especially the disconnected (Gaussian) part—requires addressing subtle effects like effective area overlap between catalogue-based fields and Poisson-like variance from discrete sampling, which motivates this work.
AI.method: The method uses the Narrow-Kernel Approximation to handle contributions from distinct source pairs to the covariance estimator, while including the noise-like self-pair contributions exactly. It accounts for effective area overlap between different catalogue-based fields and additional Poisson variance from discreteness. Results are compared to a brute-force exact covariance method for sparse samples and validated against simulations.
AI.result: The method is accurate in realistic scenarios, covering dense and noise-dominated datasets (e.g., cosmic shear) as well as sparse, noise-dominated observables (e.g., fast radio bursts). It is implemented in the public code NaMaster.
AI.conclusion: The proposed covariance estimation approach, built on the Narrow-Kernel Approximation, is validated as accurate across a wide range of cosmological datasets, offering a practical tool for uncertainty quantification in power spectrum analyses from discrete source catalogues, now available in NaMaster.

title: The Goldilocks Molecule: H$_{2}$ Emission Lines Can Identify Elusive Dwarf AGN
comment: Accepted to RNAAS
summary: We propose using H$_{2}$ emission lines as a novel diagnostic to identify dwarf AGN by running photoionization models incorporating active intermediate-mass black holes and using an observed WISE dwarf AGN as a template. Though many dwarf AGN would be incorrectly classified as star-forming if the H$_{2}$~2.12~$μ$m/Br$γ$ ratio is used, ratios between H$_{2}$ emission lines can reveal active IMBHs in cases where log $n_{\text{H}} \gtrsim 4.0$. This includes the case where $M_{\text{BH}} = 10^3~M_{\odot}$, even though the optical strong lines and NIR coronal lines would likely go undetected. We conclude that H$_{2}$ emission lines show promise in detecting the most elusive IMBHs.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes using H2 emission lines as a novel diagnostic to identify dwarf AGN with intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs), showing that H2 line ratios can reveal active IMBHs even when optical and NIR coronal lines go undetected, particularly at high hydrogen densities (log nH ≳ 4.0), including for black holes as low as 10^3 M⊙.
AI.motivation: To develop a new method for detecting elusive intermediate-mass black holes (IMBHs) in dwarf galaxies, which are difficult to identify using traditional optical strong-line diagnostics or NIR coronal lines due to their faintness.
AI.method: Running photoionization models incorporating active intermediate-mass black holes and using an observed WISE dwarf AGN as a template to analyze H2 emission line diagnostics.
AI.result: H2 2.12 μm/Brγ ratio alone misclassifies many dwarf AGN as star-forming, but ratios between different H2 emission lines can successfully identify active IMBHs when log nH ≳ 4.0, even for M_BH = 10^3 M⊙ where optical lines and NIR coronal lines remain undetected.
AI.conclusion: H2 emission lines are a promising diagnostic tool for detecting the most elusive IMBHs in dwarf galaxies.

title: CAMB v2: cosmological power spectra for high-precision surveys
comment: 25 pages, 4 figures. Code available at https://github.com/cmbant/camb
summary: Upcoming cosmic microwave background (CMB) and large-scale-structure surveys require theoretical power spectra with numerical errors well below their observational uncertainties over the scales that carry most of the constraining power. We describe a substantial update to CAMB designed to provide fast, high-precision predictions for two key outputs: the lensed CMB and matter power spectra. The central development is a new treatment of the hyperspherical Bessel functions used for line-of-sight integration in non-flat cosmologies. A leading-order Olver construction maps the curved radial equation onto the flat spherical Bessel equation by matching their actions through the turning point. The resulting approximation is exact in the flat limit, remains smooth through the turning point, and reduces near flatness to a simple rescaling of the flat Bessel argument and amplitude. We also describe updated integrators, a recalibrated fast recombination model, stabilized parameterized post-Friedmann dark-energy evolution, and improvements to CMB lensing accuracy. Numerical convergence is assessed by comparing unboosted default results against more converged calculations. The defaults meet conservative $10^{-3}$ pointwise convergence targets over the main lensed-CMB and quasi-linear matter-power ranges relevant for future surveys. Errors measured in typical runs are substantially smaller than this. We also describe the convention dependence of the nominally linear matter power spectrum when a homogeneous calculation attempts to represent the effects of reionization heating. Essentially all of the new algorithms and code were developed with LLMs or AI agents under human supervision.

AI.tldr: CAMB has been substantially updated to provide fast, high-precision predictions for lensed CMB and matter power spectra, featuring a new treatment of hyperspherical Bessel functions for non-flat cosmologies based on Olver's method, along with improved integrators, recombination models, and dark-energy evolution, achieving <10^{-3} convergence targets for future surveys. The code was developed using LLMs/AI agents under human supervision.
AI.motivation: Upcoming CMB and large-scale-structure surveys require theoretical power spectra with numerical errors well below observational uncertainties over the most constraining scales, necessitating substantial updates to existing Boltzmann codes like CAMB.
AI.method: A leading-order Olver construction maps the curved radial equation onto the flat spherical Bessel equation by matching actions through the turning point, yielding an approximation exact in the flat limit that remains smooth through the turning point. Additional updates include new integrators, a recalibrated fast recombination model, stabilized parameterized post-Friedmann dark-energy evolution, and improvements to CMB lensing accuracy.
AI.result: Default settings meet conservative 10^{-3} pointwise convergence targets over the main lensed-CMB and quasi-linear matter-power ranges relevant for future surveys; errors in typical runs are substantially smaller than this.
AI.conclusion: The updated CAMB achieves the required precision for next-generation CMB and LSS surveys, and all new algorithms and code were developed with LLMs or AI agents under human supervision.

title: Isomer-specific excitation of formic acid in collisions with helium atoms
summary: An accurate estimation of the molecular abundances of isomers in the interstellar medium (ISM) is necessary to unravel the underlying chemistry and physics. After the recent detections of both isomers of formic acid ($cis-$ and $trans-$HCOOH) in dense dark cold clouds, their accurate molecular line modeling became of interest. The conditions of these environments do not necessarily follow the local thermodynamic equilibrium, thus taking into account the competition between the radiative and collisional processes is required. This involves the knowledge of the rotational excitation data for collisions with the most abundant interstellar species \textemdash He and H$_2$. In this paper, the first potential energy surfaces (PES) for the interaction of the two rotamers of formic acid with He atoms are computed using the explicitly correlated coupled-cluster theory [CCSD(T)-F12]. The obtained PESs demonstrate qualitative similarities and high anisotropy. The global minima are found with $V=-53.0$ cm$^{-1}$ and $V=-46.0$ cm$^{-1}$ for $cis-$HCOOH and $trans-$HCOOH respectively. Collisional excitation cross sections calculated for total energies up to 100 cm$^{-1}$ demonstrate similar propensity rules for both isomers. Quantitative differences of the cross sections associated with the two rotamers are also discussed.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the first potential energy surfaces (PES) for the interaction of cis- and trans-formic acid with He atoms using CCSD(T)-F12 theory, and calculates collisional excitation cross sections up to 100 cm⁻¹, showing similar propensity rules but quantitative differences between the two isomers.
AI.motivation: Accurate modeling of molecular line emission for both isomers of formic acid (cis- and trans-HCOOH) detected in dense dark cold clouds requires knowledge of collisional (not just radiative) excitation data, which necessitates interaction potentials with the most abundant species like He and H₂.
AI.method: First potential energy surfaces (PES) for cis- and trans-HCOOH interacting with He atoms were computed using explicitly correlated coupled-cluster theory [CCSD(T)-F12]. Collisional excitation cross sections were then calculated for total energies up to 100 cm⁻¹.
AI.result: Both PESs show qualitative similarities and high anisotropy, with global minima at V = -53.0 cm⁻¹ (cis-HCOOH) and V = -46.0 cm⁻¹ (trans-HCOOH). Cross sections exhibit similar propensity rules for both isomers, with quantitative differences discussed.
AI.conclusion: The computed PESs and cross sections enable non-LTE modeling of formic acid isomers in cold dense clouds, providing essential data to distinguish their chemical pathways and abundances in the interstellar medium.

title: The VST ATLAS Survey -- IV: Galaxy, LRG and QSO bias and HODs via ACT CMB Lensing
comment: 16 pages, 16 figures, submitted to MNRAS
summary: We present angular correlation and power spectral analyses of the clustering of VST ATLAS galaxies, LRGs and QSOs and their cross-correlations with the ACT DR6 CMB lensing map with its $\approx3\times$ higher resolution than Planck DR3. We first use $Λ$CDM Halofit models at linear scales to estimate galaxy, LRG and QSO bias, $b$, from the ratio of the 3-D power spectra, $b= P_{gg}/P_{gK}$ and hence the mass clustering amplitudes, $σ_8$. For galaxies we find $b_G(z=0.15)=1.22\pm0.07$, $σ_8(z=0)=0.71\pm0.06$ and for LRGs $b_{LRG}(z=0.26)=2.76\pm0.11$, $σ_8(z=0)=0.63\pm0.15$, both consistent with $Λ$CDM predictions. But for QSOs, we estimate a bias of $b_Q(z=1.7)=4.44\pm0.24$ and $σ_8(z=0)=0.49\pm0.06$, the latter significantly lower than expected for $Λ$CDM and leads to an observed $0.15<z<1.7$ gravitational growth rate faster than predicted for $Λ$CDM. At smaller non-linear scales, HOD model fits imply a broad halo mass distribution for $z\approx0.15$ galaxies but much narrower mass distributions for LRGs and QSOs. More surprisingly, the HOD fit for QSOs implies $M_{eff}=5\times10^{14}M_\odot$, $\approx10\times$ higher than expected. Finally, while the LRG and QSO HOD models fit $w_{gg}$ and $w_{gK}$ consistently, the same is not true for the $z\approx0.15$ galaxies unless we hypothesise anti-bias with $b_G\approx0.55$. This result supports previous QSO lensing analyses that also found anti-bias at $r<5$h$^{-1}$Mpc. We suggest that while HOD + NFW halo models may well describe LRG mass profiles and clustering, at intermediate scales the dominant galaxy population (and QSOs) may follow the alternative hierarchical clustering model of \cite{Peebles1974} where galaxies trace the mass more closely than in a halo model.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes clustering of VST ATLAS galaxies, LRGs, and QSOs with ACT DR6 CMB lensing, finding consistent ΛCDM results for galaxies and LRGs, but QSOs show a lower σ₈ and faster growth rate than expected. HOD models reveal anti-bias at small scales for galaxies, suggesting alternative hierarchical clustering models may be needed.
AI.motivation: To constrain galaxy bias, σ₈, and growth rate across different tracers (galaxies, LRGs, QSOs) using higher-resolution ACT DR6 CMB lensing data, and to test ΛCDM predictions against observations.
AI.method: Angular correlation and power spectral analyses of VST ATLAS galaxies, LRGs, QSOs cross-correlated with ACT DR6 CMB lensing; linear-scale ΛCDM Halofit modeling for bias and σ₈; HOD modeling at non-linear scales.
AI.result: Galaxies: b_G=1.22±0.07, σ₈=0.71±0.06; LRGs: b_LRG=2.76±0.11, σ₈=0.63±0.15 (both consistent with ΛCDM). QSOs: b_Q=4.44±0.24, σ₈=0.49±0.06 (lower than ΛCDM, faster growth rate). HOD fits show anti-bias for galaxies at r<5 h⁻¹Mpc.
AI.conclusion: LRG HOD+NFW models work well, but galaxies and QSOs may require alternative hierarchical clustering models where mass is traced more closely than halo models predict.

title: The World Cup in space: Finding ionised buckyballs in the ISM with CARMENES
comment: To appear in Highlights of Spanish Astrophysics XIII, Proceedings of the XVII Scientific Meeting of the Spanish Astronomical Society held on 13-17 July 2026, in Tarragona, Spain
summary: Over a century after the discovery of the first diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) in absorption in stellar spectra (Heger et al 1922), their origin is still mostly unknown. The exception are four DIBs (out of 600+ known) in the 9300-9700 Angstrom region, for which a possible ascription to C_60^+ (ionised buckminsterfullerene, shaped liked a football, hence buckyballs) has been made. However, those DIBs are located in a spectral region heavily contaminated by telluric H_2O absorption, hampering their detection and study from the ground. I present the results of a study with the CARMENES spectrograph that uses a novel technique with multi-epoch spectroscopy at different times of the year to shift the relative position of the DIBs and the surrounding telluric lines, hence facilitating the analysis of the DIBs. The technique has been applied to 41 sightlines of diverse extinctions and environments, with positive detections in all of them. Our results are consistent with three of those DIBs having C_60^+ as the carrier.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a multi-epoch spectroscopic technique using CARMENES to mitigate telluric H2O contamination in the 9300-9700 Å region, enabling detection and analysis of four DIBs potentially associated with C60^+. Applied to 41 sightlines, the results confirm three DIBs likely originate from ionized buckminsterfullerene.
AI.motivation: Most of the 600+ known diffuse interstellar bands (DIBs) remain unidentified, except four in the near-infrared region possibly attributed to C60^+. However, these DIBs are heavily obscured by telluric H2O absorption from the ground, making reliable detection and study challenging.
AI.method: Multi-epoch spectroscopy with the CARMENES spectrograph at different times of the year was used to shift the relative positions of DIBs and telluric H2O lines, thereby reducing contamination. The technique was applied to 41 sightlines covering diverse extinction levels and interstellar environments.
AI.result: Positive detections of the four DIBs were obtained in all 41 sightlines. The results are consistent with three of these DIBs having C60^+ (ionized buckminsterfullerene) as their carrier.
AI.conclusion: The novel multi-epoch technique effectively mitigates telluric contamination, confirming C60^+ as the likely carrier for three DIBs in the 9300–9700 Å region, and provides a path forward for studying these bands in more sightlines.

title: High resolution Lyman-α forest constraints on dark matter-neutrino scattering
comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, comments welcome
summary: We present new constraints on models of dark matter interacting with neutrino, based on high-resolution Lyman-$α$ forest data. We perform a suite of full hydrodynamical simulations of these models, spanning a range of interaction strengths and thermal histories. We train an emulator on the simulation results. A Monte Carlo Markov Chain analysis yields an upper limit on the interaction strength of $u_{νχ} \leq1.5\times10^{-8}$ (95% C.L.), which is the strongest direct bound to date on such interactions. Our results exclude previous hints of non-zero interactions presented in the literature. We furthermore compare our results to those obtained by mapping warm dark matter constraints to other models with suppressed small-scale structure, and find that these methods would overestimate the constraining power for this model.

AI.tldr: This paper presents the strongest direct bound on dark matter-neutrino interactions ($u_{νχ} \leq 1.5\times10^{-8}$ at 95% C.L.) using Lyman-α forest data, full hydrodynamical simulations, an emulator, and MCMC analysis, while excluding previous hints of non-zero interactions and showing that mapping warm dark matter constraints overestimates constraining power.
AI.motivation: To constrain dark matter-neutrino interactions, which are poorly understood, and to address previous inconclusive hints of non-zero interactions in the literature.
AI.method: Full hydrodynamical simulations spanning various interaction strengths and thermal histories, training an emulator on simulation results, and performing Monte Carlo Markov Chain analysis against high-resolution Lyman-α forest data.
AI.result: Upper limit on interaction strength of $u_{νχ} \leq 1.5\times10^{-8}$ (95% C.L.), the strongest direct bound to date; previous hints of non-zero interactions are excluded.
AI.conclusion: The direct bound is the most stringent for dark matter-neutrino interactions, and mapping warm dark matter constraints to other models overestimates their constraining power for this specific model.

title: Berkeley 32: A Metal-poor and Dynamically Evolved Open Cluster with Evidence of Radial Migration
comment: 27 pages, including 15 figures and 4 tables, accepted for publication in the The Astronomical Journal (AJ)
summary: We present a comprehensive chemo-dynamical analysis of the old, metal-poor open cluster Berkeley 32 based on Gaia DR3 astrometry and Gaia-ESO Survey DR5.1 spectroscopy. Cluster membership is determined using a Gaussian Mixture Model applied to proper-motion components and trigonometric parallaxes. Isochrone fitting yields an age of 4.9 +/- 0.5 Gyr, a heliocentric distance of 3325 pc, and an extinction of A_V = 0.38 +/- 0.12 mag. Spectroscopic member stars exhibit a mean metallicity of [Fe/H] = -0.39 +/- 0.02 dex, near-solar alpha-element abundances, and a weighted mean radial velocity of V_rad = 106.26 +/- 0.03 km s^-1. The [Y/Mg] chemical clock yields an age of 4.73 +/- 2.39 Gyr, consistent with the isochrone estimate. Orbital integration indicates a moderately eccentric orbit (e = 0.268 +/- 0.004) with a guiding radius of R_g = 8.82 kpc. The inferred chemical birth radius, R_b = 9.82 kpc, together with DeltaR ~ -1 kpc, suggests moderate inward radial migration, while the offsets among R_b, R_g, and R_GC are consistent with both churning and blurring processes. A photometric analysis identifies a binary fraction of f_b = 0.449 +/- 0.017 for systems with mass ratios q >= 0.5, implying a substantial unresolved binary population. Radial cumulative distribution functions further reveal significant mass segregation, with evolved stars more centrally concentrated than main-sequence stars. These results indicate that Berkeley 32 is a dynamically evolved old-disk cluster whose present-day structure and orbit preserve signatures of both internal dynamical evolution and radial migration within the Galactic disk.

AI.tldr: Berkeley 32 is a 4.9 Gyr old, metal-poor ([Fe/H] = -0.39) open cluster at ~3.3 kpc with near-solar α abundances, a binary fraction of ~45%, and signatures of mass segregation and inward radial migration (~1 kpc).
AI.motivation: To characterize the chemo-dynamical properties of the old, metal-poor open cluster Berkeley 32, probing its formation, dynamical evolution, and radial migration history within the Galactic disk.
AI.method: Gaia DR3 astrometry + Gaia-ESO DR5.1 spectroscopy; Gaussian Mixture Model for membership; isochrone fitting; orbital integration; chemical clock ([Y/Mg]); radial cumulative distribution functions for mass segregation; binary fraction from photometry.
AI.result: Age = 4.9 ± 0.5 Gyr; distance = 3,325 pc; [Fe/H] = -0.39 ± 0.02 dex; V_rad = 106.26 ± 0.03 km/s; eccentricity e = 0.268; guiding radius R_g = 8.82 kpc; chemical birth radius R_b = 9.82 kpc; binary fraction f_b = 0.449 ± 0.017 (q ≥ 0.5); significant mass segregation detected.
AI.conclusion: Berkeley 32 is a dynamically evolved old-disk cluster showing evidence of internal dynamical evolution (mass segregation, binary population) and moderate inward radial migration (~1 kpc), with signatures of both churning and blurring processes.

title: Refining primordial black hole dark matter constraints with dust heating: the role of spin and halo profile dependence
comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, Comments welcome!
summary: Primordial black holes (PBHs) are compelling dark matter candidates. PBHs with masses between $10^{15}$ and $10^{18}\,\mathrm{g}$ can heat interstellar dust via Hawking radiation. Previous studies of this dust heating mechanism mostly neglected PBH spin and adopted a single dark matter halo profile. In this work, we incorporate PBH spin, which substantially enhances the emitted radiation flux, and systematically investigate the dependence of constraints on the dark matter density distribution by considering five different halo models. We compute the complete photon spectra, including both primary and secondary emissions. Our results show that, for a fixed profile and mass function, larger spin parameters yield stronger constraints on the PBH fraction $f_{\mathrm{PBH}}$. Among the halo models, the Isothermal profile gives the most stringent limits, followed by Einasto, then NFW and Moore, while the Burkert profile yields the weakest constraints. For silicate grains, which cool less efficiently than graphite, the upper limits reach $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ for high spin cases. We consider both monochromatic and lognormal mass functions, and find consistent trends between them. For the lognormal case, larger values of the width $σ$ lead to a broader mass range being excluded, in particular ruling out massive PBHs as the sole dark matter component. Our bounds are generally weaker than other existing limits, but they provide a complementary and independent constraint.

AI.tldr: This paper incorporates PBH spin and five different dark matter halo models to constrain the PBH fraction via dust heating from Hawking radiation, finding that larger spin yields stronger constraints, the Isothermal profile is most restrictive, and silicate grains give upper limits as low as ~10⁻⁴.
AI.motivation: Primordial black holes (PBHs) are compelling dark matter candidates, and previous studies of PBH heating of interstellar dust via Hawking radiation mostly neglected PBH spin and adopted a single dark matter halo profile. This work aims to address these gaps.
AI.method: Incorporated PBH spin (which enhances emitted radiation flux), systematically investigated five different halo models (Isothermal, Einasto, NFW, Moore, Burkert), computed complete photon spectra including primary and secondary emissions, and considered both monochromatic and lognormal mass functions.
AI.result: Larger spin parameters yield stronger constraints on f_PBH. Isothermal profile gives the most stringent limits, followed by Einasto, NFW, Moore, with Burkert weakest. For silicate grains, upper limits reach O(10⁻⁴) for high spin. For lognormal mass function, larger width σ excludes broader mass ranges, ruling out massive PBHs as sole DM component.
AI.conclusion: The bounds are generally weaker than other existing limits but provide complementary and independent constraints on PBHs as dark matter candidates.

title: Cluster characteristics of Galactic open clusters
comment: 11 pages, 17 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: Star clusters are perfectly suited for studying the formation, evolution, and dynamics of stars and their host galaxies. For this, we need to estimate total masses, radii and shapes of star clusters. These parameters strongly influence their fates in the host galaxies. However, there is no agreement about these characteristics in the literature. The published values widely disagree. We estimated total masses and cluster radii using a very conservative approach: calculating member masses and summing them. Furthermore, we investigated the three-dimensional characteristics of open clusters and their limitations. We used a commonly used grid of evolutionary tracks for different photometric sources, including 2MASS, Gaia, and Pan-STARRS. The interpolation method was tested using synthetic clusters built with ASteCA. To estimate three-dimensional shapes, we used the distribution of the well-known Galactic coordinates and inverse parallaxes. We estimated the total masses and radii of about 7000 open clusters and observed traces of tidal tails. Individual values can be used in future $Gaia$ data releases to obtain even more precise values. The current DR3 allows the study of only three-dimensional shapes up to 500 pc. Beyond this distance, we find a significant needle-like shape due to uncertainties in observed parallaxes.

AI.tldr: This paper studies ~7000 open clusters, estimating total masses, radii, and 3D shapes using a conservative member-summing approach with evolutionary tracks from 2MASS, Gaia, and Pan-STARRS. Three-dimensional shape analysis is reliable only within 500 pc; beyond that, parallax uncertainties introduce artificial needle-like shapes. Traces of tidal tails are observed.
AI.motivation: Star cluster parameters (mass, radius, shape) are crucial for understanding stellar and galactic evolution, yet published values for these characteristics are highly inconsistent and disagree widely in the literature.
AI.method: Conservative approach: summing individual member masses. Used evolutionary track grids from 2MASS, Gaia, and Pan-STARRS; interpolation tested with synthetic clusters via ASteCA. 3D shapes estimated from Galactic coordinates and inverse parallaxes.
AI.result: Total masses and radii estimated for ~7000 open clusters; tidal tail traces found. 3D shapes only reliable within 500 pc; beyond that, parallax uncertainties produce artificial needle-like shapes.
AI.conclusion: Current Gaia DR3 enables 3D shape studies only up to 500 pc; future data releases may yield more precise values. Individual cluster parameters are provided for future use.

title: Cosmic string gravitational wave backgrounds at LISA: II. Reconstruction of conventional signals over astrophysical foregrounds
comment: 19 pages + 8 figures
summary: We study the reconstruction of conventional cosmic-string signals with LISA in the presence of all major known astrophysical foregrounds expected in the LISA band. These include stellar-origin black-hole binaries (SOBHBs), galactic (WDs) and extragalactic (ExWDs) white dwarfs, extreme-mass-ratio-inspirals (EMRIs), and massive black-hole binaries (MBHBs). Using the Simulation-based Inference package GWBackFinder, we perform a joint inference on the LISA noise, foregrounds, and signal, across a range of injected string tensions $Gμ$. We find that reconstructing tensions with an error $\lesssim 10\%$ requires values as large as $Gμ\gtrsim 10^{-11}$, i.e. a factor $\sim10^5$ larger than previous estimates with no foregrounds, and $\sim 10^2$ larger compared to estimates accounting only for SOBHB and WD foregrounds. This work is the second in a series initiated in Ref. arXiv:2508.05395, which aims to quantify LISA's ability to measure representative cosmic-string models.

AI.tldr: This paper studies the reconstruction of cosmic-string signals with LISA, finding that realistic astrophysical foregrounds (SOBHBs, WDs, ExWDs, EMRIs, MBHBs) significantly degrade sensitivity, requiring Gμ ≳ 10⁻¹¹ for ≤10% error—~10⁵ times larger than no-foreground estimates.
AI.motivation: To quantify LISA's ability to measure conventional cosmic-string signals under realistic conditions with all major astrophysical foregrounds simultaneously.
AI.method: Joint inference on LISA noise, foregrounds (SOBHBs, WDs, ExWDs, EMRIs, MBHBs), and cosmic-string signal using the Simulation-based Inference package GWBackFinder across a range of injected string tensions Gμ.
AI.result: Reconstructing tensions with ≤10% error requires Gμ ≳ 10⁻¹¹, which is ~10⁵ larger than no-foreground estimates and ~10² larger than estimates with only SOBHB and WD foregrounds.
AI.conclusion: Realistic foregrounds dramatically degrade LISA's sensitivity to cosmic strings compared to earlier optimistic estimates, making detection feasible only for relatively high-tension strings.
